mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows unauthenticated (non-AuthenticatedMember) members to be task creators and deleters. The assertion mandates that all creators and deleters are authenticated; without this fact, Alloy can model an instance where an unauthenticated member creates a task, directly violating the security boundary.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthenticatedCreator { some t: Task | t.creator not in AuthenticatedMember }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the unique-task-id constraint allows the same task_id to appear in multiple TaskDeletion records, violating the append-only invariant that each deletion log entry records a distinct task.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DuplicateDeletion { some disj td1, td2: TaskDeletion | td1.deleted_task_id = td2.deleted_task_id }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows unauthenticated members to hold operations in the permission matrix, violating the least-privilege principle that only authenticated members have any access rights.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthenticatedPermission { some m: Member - AuthenticatedMember, op: Operation | (m -> op) in PermMatrix.allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows authenticated members to have differentiated permission sets, violating the specification's flat-peer-model requirement that all members have identical permissions.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DifferentiatedPermissions { some m1, m2: AuthenticatedMember, op: Operation | ((m1 -> op) in PermMatrix.allowed) and ((m2 -> op) not in PermMatrix.allowed) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the explicit definition of the permission matrix allows it to be incomplete or inconsistent. The assertion checks that every authenticated member has all four operations; without this fact, Alloy can model a member lacking a permission.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_IncompletePermissions { some m: AuthenticatedMember | (m -> CreateOp) not in PermMatrix.allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the status constraint allows tasks to hold values outside {TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE}, violating the requirement that every task has a valid status from the allowed set.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InvalidStatus { some t: Task | t.status not in (TODO + IN_PROGRESS + DONE) }
